_meta.question: When can I take 1, 2 or 3 weeks off with no games in this section?

interpretations.strict: Spring Training exhibitions count as MLB games.
interpretations.regular: Only MLB regular season and postseason count.

_meta.method: For each section and calendar year we block (a) the previous NFL season's precise Week 17/18 and playoff dates plus the Pro Bowl Games, (b) that year's MLB games - exact official fixture dates when the committed league snapshot for that year exists, otherwise the documented continuous season frame, (c) that year's NFL season from the Hall of Fame Game to Dec 31, (d) in sections 2-3 the Stanford/California football span, (e) in section 3 the Earthquakes MLS span, and (f) in the superset only the Warriors NBA and Valkyries WNBA spans. We then report every contiguous unblocked run and whether it satisfies 1, 2 or 3 weeks.
_meta.caveat: Continuous season envelopes are conservative and can hide real fixture gaps. No candidate found is not proof a trip is impossible. Future schedule and radio coverage remain incomplete.

comparison_notes: [Spring Training counts] Section 1 - MLB + NFL: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[Spring Training counts] Section 2 - Section 1 + Stanford/Cal football: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[Spring Training counts] Section 3 - Section 2 + Earthquakes MLS: longest run across the four years is 11 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 1/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[Spring Training counts] The sections do NOT agree (Section 1 11 d, Section 2 11 d, Section 3 11 d). Section 1 is the binding constraint.

[regular season + postseason only] Section 1 - MLB + NFL: longest run across the four years is 44 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 4/4, 3 weeks in 4/4. 3-week years: 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029.

[regular season + postseason only] Section 2 - Section 1 + Stanford/Cal football: longest run across the four years is 44 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 4/4 years, 2 weeks in 4/4, 3 weeks in 4/4. 3-week years: 2026, 2027, 2028, 2029.
[regular season + postseason only] Section 3 - Section 2 + Earthquakes MLS: longest run across the four years is 12 days; a 1-week candidate is found in 1/4 years, 2 weeks in 0/4, 3 weeks in 0/4.
[regular season + postseason only] The sections do NOT agree (Section 1 44 d, Section 2 44 d, Section 3 12 d). Section 3 is the binding constraint.

Sections 1 and 2 have matching longest modeled runs in (2026, 2027, 2028, 2029, both readings). Bay Area college football adds a conditional December/January bowl and CFP envelope, which is conditional on Stanford or Cal qualifying and never creates or destroys a 1-, 2- or 3-week window. In this model the longest run is unchanged; daily free hours can still differ.

Adding the San Jose Earthquakes is the only change that costs a whole trip - 2027 (strict): 8 d -> 5 d; 2028 (strict): 8 d -> 5 d; 2029 (strict): 8 d -> 5 d; 2026 (regular): 44 d -> 12 d; 2027 (regular): 37 d -> 5 d; 2028 (regular): 40 d -> 5 d; 2029 (regular): 41 d -> 5 d. MLS changes to a summer–spring calendar in 2027. Conservative phase envelopes are used, which may hide actual fixture gaps. For 2–3 weeks away, no Section 3 candidate is found in this model; Sections 1 and 2 have candidates.

The reading of 'no MLB games' matters more than the section does. If Spring Training counts, the best week in any year is the 8-11 days between the conference championships and the Pro Bowl, and no section reaches two weeks. If only the regular season and postseason count, Sections 1 and 2 open a 5-6 week corridor from the day after the Super Bowl to Opening Day, and only Section 3 misses out.
